Definition: properly, a step; by implication, a steep or inaccessible place
BiblicalUsage: Madregah is a step, a steep place, a stair, and it appears twice. Ezekiel 38:20 has the steep places falling when the mountains are thrown down, and Song of Solomon 2:14 calls the beloved to come out of the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that the same word holds both judgments: steep places fall, and a hidden love is called out of them.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
